$comment: Acceptance criteria for issue 197. Two installs on one machine reported version=0.4.1 and differed by four merges; the stale one was missing conformance/roadmap.py, the split_to pointers and ADR-033. engine/version.py moves on a release and installs are made whenever, so the version string cannot distinguish two installs and it is the only version-shaped thing an install carries. The two install paths make different promises: the documented one clones --branch <tag>; tools/install-skill.sh clones the installing machine's checkout at whatever HEAD it is on, so an install made from a feature branch carries unmerged code and reports the released version number. INSTALLED.md is written precisely to explain the install to whoever finds it -- it lists every pruned path -- and records no commit and no date. THE VACUITY THIS BAR IS BUILT AGAINST is asserting against a hand-written fixture: only a DRIVEN install proves the script writes the provenance. CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE: it says 'the suite already drives the installer into temp repositories, so the seam exists' -- conformance/install.py does NOT (grep for install-skill returns nothing there; it asks the REMOTE whether the documented tag exists, per issue 178). The installer is driven by conformance/skill.py, hooks.py, benchmark.py and onboarding.py, so the pattern exists to copy but the seam must be built here. A check that reads a committed sample INSTALLED.md passes forever without the installer changing. C4 is the second direction: an implementation that hardcodes 'not a tag' satisfies C3 and lies whenever the source IS on a tag. WHAT THIS BAR DOES NOT DECIDE: whether the script should refuse, or merely warn, when the source checkout is dirty or on a feature branch. The issue names that as a separate judgement and does not assume it; recording provenance is closeable without settling it.

criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/install.py | grep -q "\[PASS\].*a driven install records the source commit"'
criteria.$comment: C1 THE DEFECT. The installer is RUN and the INSTALLED.md it produces names the commit it came from. Red today.

criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/install.py | grep -q "\[PASS\].*and the branch and the install date"'
criteria.$comment: C2 The other two facts a reader needs to tell two installs apart. A commit alone does not say whether it was ever merged.

criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/install.py | grep -q "\[PASS\].*an install from an untagged source says so"'
criteria.$comment: C3 The case where the version string is least trustworthy is named plainly, rather than left for a reader to infer from a hash.

criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/install.py | grep -q "\[PASS\].*an install from a tag names the tag"'
criteria.$comment: C4 THE SECOND DIRECTION. Without it, hardcoding the untagged warning satisfies C3 while telling every tagged install something false.

C5 DRIVEN, NOT READ. The assertion must run the installer rather than inspect a checked-in sample, or it vouches for provenance the script never wrote. Red today and correctly so: install.py drives nothing. Four other suites already drive install-skill.sh into temp repositories -- copy one.
